Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but Democratic nominee Chevalier is heavily favored

model.rationale: This Upper Manhattan seat carries a +32 Democratic partisan lean, and the Democratic nominee has outraised and outspent her Republican opponent by enormous margins, with outside groups heavily engaged on her side. Prediction markets price the Democrat near 97%, so the only real question is the size of the margin, which should land in the low-to-mid 30s.
model.watch: A surprisingly weak Democratic primary outcome or unusually low turnout in a low-profile open seat could shave a few points off the margin, though not the expected winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-13 is a heavily Democratic Upper Manhattan district with a +32 partisan lean. Adriano Espaillat is not on the ballot after losing renomination, leaving Darializa Avila Chevalier as the Democratic nominee against Republican Jomo Williams in an open-seat contest.

Chevalier has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $1.9 million in outside support, while Williams shows no meaningful fundraising or outside spending. Prediction markets price the Democrat at 97%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the low-to-mid 30s margin range.
